# ankra_pipeline_definition (Resource)

The definition of record of a repository's Ankra pipeline, stored from a spec rather than read from the committed `.ankra/pipeline.yaml`. The counterpart of `ankra pipeline definition put` and `ankra application pipeline definition put`. The platform stores a canonical render of the spec, so drift is detected by `spec_hash`. A later push of the committed file records a new definition, which Terraform then shows as drift. The platform cannot delete a definition: destroying this resource only removes it from Terraform state.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "ankra_pipeline_definition" "platform" {
  repository_id = ankra_pipeline_repository.platform.id
  spec_yaml     = file("${path.module}/pipeline.yaml")
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `spec_yaml` (String) Pipeline spec, in the `.ankra/pipeline.yaml` format, stored as the definition of record.

### Optional

- `application_id` (String) Application whose linked repository the definition belongs to. Set exactly one of `application_id` and `repository_id`. Changing it replaces the resource.
- `repository_id` (String) Connected repository that the definition belongs to. Set exactly one of `application_id` and `repository_id`. Changing it replaces the resource.

### Read-Only

- `protected_hash` (String) Digest of the definition's protected sections, which an administrator approves with `ankra pipeline definitions approve`.
- `source` (String) Where the definition of record came from.
- `spec_hash` (String) Hash of the canonical spec the platform stored. A different definition of record, from a push of the committed file or a put outside Terraform, shows as a change to `spec_yaml`.
- `violations` (List of String) Warnings the platform reported for the stored spec.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Imported by application/<application_id> or repository/<repository_id>.
terraform import ankra_pipeline_definition.platform repository/3c7e1b2a-4d5f-4a6b-8c9d-0e1f2a3b4c5d
```
